target_customer: Online merchants and apps that need to verify a customer physically holds a payment card or photo ID
problem: Card-not-present fraud and false declines: merchants had to block risky transactions without proof the buyer held the card.
business_model: B2B SDK and API for card and ID scanning and verification (pricing not found)
product_category: Payments fraud prevention and identity verification SDK

founders.name: Sam King
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page. UC Davis computer science news item about the company mentions Sam King, not opened in full.

technical_complexity.rationale: On-device card and ID capture with computer vision plus a sub-400 millisecond risk assessment is real engineering, but built on mature mobile vision techniques.

defensibility.rationale: Established scanning SDKs existed and no proprietary data moat is sourced; value was largely the team and tech integrated into Stripe Radar.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Stripe acquired Bouncer in May 2021 and folded the technology into Radar.

market_need_then: Card fraud and false positives in online payments were a recognized pain; Stripe cited reducing false positives on high risk transactions as the purpose of the deal.

branding.domain_note: Used getbouncer.com rather than bouncer.com (site returned HTTP 503 at fetch time). A Polish email-verification company also uses the name Bouncer.

identity.logo: A letter B mark (per a Village.ai listing)

brand_strength.rationale: Evocative gatekeeper metaphor fits the job, but no press or community about the brand itself and the name is shared with another company.

outcome_analysis: Bouncer built card and photo ID scanning for fraud-sensitive merchants out of Oakland and went through YC in Summer 2019. Stripe announced the acquisition on 14 May 2021 to strengthen Radar, with the team and technology joining Stripe and terms undisclosed. Funding is not public beyond aggregator entries without amounts, so whether it was a strong exit relative to capital raised is unknown.
notes: CB Insights reportedly lists seed rounds in Aug 2019 and Dec 2019 with amounts blank; unverified, not recorded as rounds. Latka bootstrapped claim ignored as unreliable. No dated competitor sources near the batch were found, only undated vendor pages (Card.io, Microblink, Jumio), so the list is empty. Founder education not found.
